command.description: The brief provider command, split on whitespace with no shell. phax writes a brief request on its stdin and reads a brief report {"$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/brief-report/<release>.json", "rules", "findings"} on stdout: the rules over the requested paths, and the findings there with their due. A provider that declines to run exits non-zero. A brief informs and never blocks. Full contract: `phax --usage`, cmd brief.

push.description: What the phase's first prompt lists from the phase's brief, at most 50 lines. "findings": the findings due in this phase. "findings-and-rules": those findings, then the rules over the phase's planned files, with their files and guides. Required, with no default, in every layer that declares brief.

brief.description: The brief provider: a command that answers, for any paths, the rules over them and what fails there. phax pushes the phase's brief into the phase's first prompt and serves `phax brief`.

command.description: The plan auditor command. The string is split on whitespace with no shell — use a wrapper script for paths with spaces or pipelines. phax writes the plan projection ({"phases": [{"id", "files"}]}) to the provider's stdin from `phax plans lint` whenever the plan's deterministic extraction succeeds, and expects exit 0 with {"findings": [{"message", "phases": [...]}]} on stdout. Every finding is a warning on the lint's advisory check, one per phase it names; a failing auditor is one warning, and the command is capped at 30s; findings never set the exit code. `phax run` never queries it. Full contract: `phax --usage`, cmd plans lint.

The architecture provider command. The string is split on whitespace with no shell — use a wrapper script for paths with spaces or pipelines. phax writes an architecture request {"$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/architecture-request/<release>.json", "files"} to its stdin and reads an architecture report {"$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/architecture-report/<release>.json", "body", "parts"} on stdout, which phax renders to Markdown; a provider that declines exits non-zero. Full contract: `phax --usage`, cmd architecture.

architecture.description: The architecture provider: a command that answers, for the whole repository or for some paths, the repository's architecture as a report (a Markdown body, then the parts of the code with their globs), which phax renders to Markdown. Serves `phax architecture`.

command.description: The acceptance provider command. The string is split on whitespace with no shell — use a wrapper script for paths with spaces or pipelines. At the gate of an acceptance phase or its passing phase only, phax writes an acceptance request {"$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/acceptance-request/<release>.json", "verdict", "phase", "acceptancePhase", "base", "files"} (plus "acceptanceCommit" on a "passed" request) to its stdin, and judges the gate report the provider prints on stdout exactly like an `output: "gate-report"` step, with a fixed 120 s limit. `phax plans lint`, `phax validate`, the run preflight and authoring never run it. Full contract: `phax --usage`, cmd run.

acceptance.description: The acceptance provider: a command that judges the acceptance tests an acceptance phase writes and its passing phase passes.

enabled.description: Run the headless code review when a run reaches review, after the compliance review and before the pull request. False when absent.

output.description: "log" (default) streams raw command output. "gate-report": phax reads a gate report {"$schema": "https://docs.phax.run/schemas/gate-report/<release>.json", "outcome": "checked", "findings", "review"} on stdout, judges the step from it and saves it as printed as checks-attempt-NN.report-SS.json, SS being the step's position among the steps the attempt runs. Any finding fails the step whatever the exit code; an empty list passes on exit 0; anything else is a broken step that fails with the raw log. A report step does not have to declare input.

input.description: Absent: the step's stdin is not connected. "gate-request": phax writes the gate request {$schema, phase, base, terminal, phases} on the step's stdin and saves it as checks-attempt-NN.request.json.

files.description: Checks the files the agent chooses. Holds a <name> placeholder (a lowercase word in angle brackets, for example <files>) that the agent replaces with those files. Commands are joined with | only.

diff.description: Checks the phase's current, uncommitted changes. Holds no placeholder. Commands are joined with | only.

partial.description: Commands that check part of what this step checks. phax shows them in the phase prompt under the step and allows them in secure mode like the step, and never runs them.

assignments.description: The repository owner's assignment bounds: an ordered, non-empty list of part and globs bounds, each with a model and an effort range, from most to least demanding. The first bound that matches any of a phase's planned files governs it; `phax plans lint` and the `phax run` / `phax resume` start preflight hold every phase to it. Accepted in phax.json only: a user overlay that carries it is refused.

part.description: The id of an architecture-report part: the bound covers the files of the part whose id this is, read from the architecture provider.

model.description: The model a governed phase takes: a catalog model id, never ranked against another.

effort.description: The efforts a phase may take, inclusive, in the order of the bound model's catalog `efforts` list. `min` equal to `max` admits one effort.

globs.description: The files the bound covers, as globs: working-tree-root-relative POSIX paths, matched case-sensitively and the same on every host. `**` as a whole segment matches zero or more segments, `*` matches zero or more characters within a segment, `?` matches one character other than `/`. A leading dot is not special. Every other character is literal, `[`, `]` and `!` included. Braces are refused. A glob covers files: write `src/core/**` to cover a directory.

items.description: Checked by phax's parser: no leading /, backslash, brace, backtick or control character, no empty, . or .. segment, and ** only as a whole segment.

model.description: The model a governed phase takes: a catalog model id, never ranked against another.

effort.description: The efforts a phase may take, inclusive, in the order of the bound model's catalog `efforts` list. `min` equal to `max` admits one effort.

items.description: Checked by phax's parser: no leading /, backslash, brace, backtick or control character, no empty, . or .. segment, and ** only as a whole segment.

protectedPaths.description: The files whose change is the operator's decision, which no phase of a run may create, change, delete or rename. The phax.json phax loads is protected too, by its repo-relative path. Accepted in phax.json only: a user overlay that carries it is refused. Globs are written in phax's glob dialect but matched ignoring letter case: working-tree-root-relative POSIX paths, matched case-sensitively and the same on every host. `**` as a whole segment matches zero or more segments, `*` matches zero or more characters within a segment, `?` matches one character other than `/`. A leading dot is not special. Every other character is literal, `[`, `]` and `!` included. Braces are refused. A glob covers files: write `src/core/**` to cover a directory.
